conceptual assets.information: The runtime enable setting determines whether the clock divider advances and whether downstream clock-enable events are generated. Clocked downstream functions depend on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: enable_i is sampled into en at line 129, and en controls whether cnt advances at lines 130-134, so changing the setting changes clock generation. Availability: disabling or corrupting the setting can prevent cnt from advancing and withhold clk_en_o events at lines 130-147.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter enable_i or the sampled en value so that the divider remains stopped and downstream logic no longer receives required clock-enable events.

conceptual assets.information: These are the divided clock-enable events generated for downstream modules. Their presence and timing pace the operation of the modules receiving clk_en_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: clk_en_o is generated directly from cnt and cnt2 at lines 140-147, so altering the divider state or decode can produce incorrect enable events. Availability: blocking or suppressing the generated events at lines 140-147 can stop downstream clocked functions from progressing.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt cnt, cnt2, or the output decode so that required clock-enable pulses are changed or withheld, disrupting downstream operation.

considered, not kept.reason: Lines 44-59 and 68-73 only combine, synchronize, and release reset requests; reset requests, their copies, reset-chain state, and reset outputs are excluded by the clocks-and-resets rule.
NUM_EN and the divider constants used at lines 102-109 and 140-147 only fix build-time structure or rates and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
